_comment: Toolchain pin for the signoff/ flow (`klt signoff --manifest`), the
signoff/ analogue of layout/toolchain.json's DRC/LVS pin and
sim/toolchain.json's ngspice/PDK pin. Checked, not merely recorded:
`python3 signoff/run_signoff.py --regen` refuses to mint a report from a
`klt` whose `klt version --format json` identity does not match the
three pinned fields below.
WHY THIS PIN IS A COMMIT AND NOT A VERSION NUMBER, and why the released
wheel is not enough: the T1 checklist grew an ELEVENTH item on
2026-09-17 (klayout-tools#2025, `Power delivery (structural)`). `klt
signoff` parses the item list out of docs/design-evidence-tiers.md
rather than duplicating it in code, and a wheel bundles a copy of that
doc as package data -- so the released `klt 0.5.0` on PyPI-equivalent
install grades a TEN-item checklist and renders NO item-11 row at all.
Verified directly while writing this pin: the release's bundled doc
(sha256:3fecfa90a3a2300e9c810734ed74f7d6e7f947b33afc48dc928cae68a46bb9c3)
stops at item 10 and its report reads `T1: 6/20 items met`; the pinned
build below reads `T1: 6/22 items met` (eleven items x two partitions)
against the doc hash recorded as `source_doc_content_hash`.
Grading against a NEWER doc with an OLDER build (`--tiers-doc` /
$KLT_TIERS_DOC) is deliberately NOT how this repo closes that gap:
klayout-tools#2176 makes such a row render
`unmet`/`ungradeable_by_build` -- an item parsed from a doc whose
grading rules the build does not have. Pinning the build is the honest
fix; overriding the doc would only move where the hole is.
klt_install               `pip install` VCS URL with an exact `@<sha>`,
not a floating branch -- same reasoning
layout/toolchain.json gives at length: an
upstream grading-rule change is something
this repo's committed verdicts absorb
deliberately, in one reviewed change, not
silently on the next reinstall.
klt_git_commit            the commit `klt_install` resolves to, restated
so it is readable without parsing the URL, and
asserted against `klt version`'s own
`git_commit` before a report is minted.
klt_version               `klt version`'s `version` string for that
commit (package version + short sha).
grading_ruleset_id        klayout-tools#2201's identity for the grading
RULES themselves. Two builds with the same
package_version can grade differently; this
field is what moves when they do.
source_doc_content_hash   sha256 of the docs/design-evidence-tiers.md
the pinned build parsed -- i.e. WHAT THE
CHECKLIST SAID when the committed report was
minted (klayout-tools#2175). A checklist
revision upstream moves this and nothing else,
which is exactly the signal that a re-read is
due.
minimum_upstream_issue    the upstream change below which this repo's
report would be missing a checklist item
outright, recorded so a future bump can tell
'newer' from 'new enough'.
Bumping this pin is a reviewed change: re-run `--regen`, read the diff of
the committed report row by row, and write what moved (and why) into the
new evidence record under signoff/records/ -- the same discipline
layout/toolchain.json's own bump paragraphs document.
